name: The Sabbath traders of Jerusalem and Tyre
charge: Treading winepresses on the Sabbath, bringing in sheaves, lading asses with wine, grapes, and figs, and bringing burdens into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day; men of Tyre selling fish and all manner of ware on the Sabbath to the children of Judah
summary: After the people had sworn not to buy wares or food from the peoples of the land on the Sabbath, Nehemiah found men of Judah treading winepresses and carrying burdens into Jerusalem on the Sabbath, and men of Tyre selling fish and all kinds of ware to the children of Judah (Nehemiah 10:31; Nehemiah 13:15-16). He contended with the nobles for profaning the Sabbath, had the gates shut at dark before it, and warned the merchants lodging outside the wall that he would lay hands on them, and they came no more on the Sabbath (Nehemiah 13:17-22).
offenseFull: When the covenant was sealed, the people swore that if the peoples of the land brought wares or food to sell on the Sabbath or a holy day, they would not buy (Nehemiah 10:31). But in those days Nehemiah saw some in Judah treading winepresses on the Sabbath, bringing in sheaves, loading donkeys, and carrying wine, grapes, figs, and all kinds of burdens into Jerusalem to sell, and men of Tyre living there sold fish and all manner of ware on the Sabbath to the children of Judah (Nehemiah 13:15-16). While Nehemiah was away the rulers had again let the other nations come in. The class likens the Tyrians to the merchants who move into our communities today and make their money off of us.

The commandment says to remember the Sabbath day and keep it holy, doing no work on the seventh day, not you, your son, your daughter, your servants, or your cattle (Exodus 20:8-10). It says remember because Israel would forget it, and in this captivity it was lost through forced conversion. The Sabbath is a sign between the Most High and the children of Israel for ever, not between Him and the other nations (Exodus 31:13-17). Jeremiah had warned this same city to carry no burden in through the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath (Jeremiah 17:21-22), the very burdens Nehemiah later shut the gates against. The same heart is recorded in Amos, where Israel asked when the new moon and the Sabbath would be gone so that they could sell corn (Amos 8:5). No buying, no selling, and no burdens on the Sabbath day.
judgmentFull: Nehemiah contended with the nobles of Judah and asked what evil thing this was, that they profaned the Sabbath. Did their fathers not do the same, so that God brought all this evil on them and on the city, and now they were bringing more wrath on Israel (Nehemiah 13:17-18)? The teaching says we had gone into captivity for breaking God’s law, and on the return there were people trying to get us to sin again. When the gates of Jerusalem began to be dark before the Sabbath he commanded them shut until after the Sabbath and set his own servants at them, so that no burden would come in (Nehemiah 13:19). The class takes from this that the Sabbath begins when it gets dark and runs from evening to evening (Leviticus 23:32), not from sunrise.

The merchants and sellers lodged outside Jerusalem once or twice, waiting to get in, and he testified against them: if they did it again he would lay hands on them (Nehemiah 13:20-21). This laying on of hands is not a blessing but a serious warning, and the merchants knew he was not joking; the teaching says our forefathers did not play games with the other nations, and from that time they came no more on the Sabbath. The captains add that the prophets of God were not soft, like the pastor who stays inside. Nehemiah commanded the Levites to cleanse themselves and keep the gates to sanctify the Sabbath day, and asked God to remember him and spare him according to the greatness of His mercy (Nehemiah 13:22).

lawsResolved.text: No buying, selling or marketing is to transpire on the Sabbath.
No burdens to be carried on during the Sabbath.
The Sabbath to be kept holy.
We are not to seek our own pleasure on the Sabbath.

text.text: And if the people of the land bring ware or any victuals on the sabbath day to sell, that we would not buy it of them on the sabbath, or on the holy day: and that we would leave the seventh year, and the exaction of every debt.

In those days saw I in Judah some treading wine presses on the sabbath, and bringing in sheaves, and lading asses; as also wine, grapes, and figs, and all manner of burdens, which they brought into Jerusalem on the sabbath day: and I testified against them in the day wherein they sold victuals.
There dwelt men of Tyre also therein, which brought fish, and all manner of ware, and sold on the sabbath unto the children of Judah, and in Jerusalem.
Then I contended with the nobles of Judah, and said unto them, What evil thing is this that ye do, and profane the sabbath day?
Did not your fathers thus, and did not our God bring all this evil upon us, and upon this city? yet ye bring more wrath upon Israel by profaning the sabbath.

And it came to pass, that when the gates of Jerusalem began to be dark before the sabbath, I commanded that the gates should be shut, and charged that they should not be opened till after the sabbath: and some of my servants set I at the gates, that there should no burden be brought in on the sabbath day.
So the merchants and sellers of all kind of ware lodged without Jerusalem once or twice.
Then I testified against them, and said unto them, Why lodge ye about the wall? if ye do so again, I will lay hands on you. From that time forth came they no more on the sabbath.

And I commanded the Levites that they should cleanse themselves, and that they should come and keep the gates, to sanctify the sabbath day. Remember me, O my God, concerning this also, and spare me according to the greatness of thy mercy.
Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.
Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work:

But the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates:

Speak thou also unto the children of Israel, saying, Verily my sabbaths ye shall keep: for it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations; that ye may know that I am the Lord that doth sanctify you.

Ye shall keep the sabbath therefore; for it is holy unto you: every one that defileth it shall surely be put to death: for whosoever doeth any work therein, that soul shall be cut off from among his people.
Six days may work be done; but in the seventh is the sabbath of rest, holy to the Lord: whosoever doeth any work in the sabbath day, he shall surely be put to death.
Wherefore the children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant.
It is a sign between me and the children of Israel for ever: for in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed.
Thus saith the Lord; Take heed to yourselves, and bear no burden on the sabbath day, nor bring it in by the gates of Jerusalem;
Neither carry forth a burden out of your houses on the sabbath day, neither do ye any work, but hallow ye the sabbath day, as I commanded your fathers.
Saying, When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell corn? and the sabbath, that we may set forth wheat, making the ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit?

It shall be unto you a sabbath of rest, and ye shall afflict your souls: in the ninth day of the month at even, from even unto even, shall ye celebrate your sabbath.

And it shall come to pass, if ye diligently hearken unto me, saith the Lord, to bring in no burden through the gates of this city on the sabbath day, but hallow the sabbath day, to do no work therein;

Then shall there enter into the gates of this city kings and princes sitting upon the throne of David, riding in chariots and on horses, they, and their princes, the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem: and this city shall remain for ever.

And they shall come from the cities of Judah, and from the places about Jerusalem, and from the land of Benjamin, and from the plain, and from the mountains, and from the south, bringing burnt offerings, and sacrifices, and meat offerings, and incense, and bringing sacrifices of praise, unto the house of the Lord.
